glasses_3d: I look at the sunrise through the 3D glasses. Red and cyan. ...I take them off. It's just a sunrise.

LOOK.text: The sun comes up. I wait for it to dip. It does not. It is just the sun.

USE.text: I let the sunrise wash over me. No screen, no candles. Just light. It doesn't want anything from me.

TALK.text: I whisper to the dawn: 'Good morning.' For the first time in months, I mean it.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a sunrise. I can carry the moment, though. It weighs nothing. Nice change.

OPEN.text: The sky opens itself every morning. No PIN, no keycard, no DOORIS. Just patience.

CLOSE.text: I close my eyes against the light. The warmth stays. Some things don't need a backup.

PUSH.text: I can't push the sun. It's coming up at its own pace. I'm learning that's allowed.

PULL.text: The sunrise pulls me toward the edge. I resist. Detective rule one: admire views from a safe distance.

GIVE.text: I offer the sun a nod. It gives back warmth, light and a slight squint. Fair trade.

LOOK.text: The clinic door behind me. I don't need to go back in.
A new sign hangs on the door: 'PATIENT ZERO REHABILITATION CLINIC — NOW HIRING'.
Hiring? Maybe Adrian's note was more literal than I thought.

USE.text: No. Forward, not back. The ecosystem needs builders, not patients.

OPEN.text: I've seen what's inside. Time to see what's outside.

TALK.text: 'Goodbye, clinic.' It gave me answers I wasn't looking for. And a wristband. Mostly answers.

PICK.text: I've taken enough from that clinic. Three weeks, a backup and a wristband.

CLOSE.text: The door's already shut. Some rooms you only need to visit once. That one, I've visited twice.

PUSH.text: I push the door firmly closed. It latches with a quiet click. Goodbye, Patient Zero.

PULL.text: Something pulls me back toward the door. Nostalgia? Fear? No. Wind. Keep walking, Dex.

GIVE.text: I'd leave a thank-you card, but Nurse Gwei would make me fill in a form for it.

LOOK.text: The world stretches out below. Somewhere down there, the FloorEngine sweeps. TraitLab creates. SweepBot runs.
Adrian's ecosystem doesn't need Adrian. It runs on code, community, and stubborn optimism.

USE.text: I breathe in the mountain air. It tastes like freedom. And pine needles. Mostly pine needles.

TALK.text: 'Thanks for keeping the clinic's secrets.' The mountains say nothing. They're very good at this.

PICK.text: I can't take the view with me. This time I'll keep the memory. No floppy required.

OPEN.text: The view is already wide open. No paywall. No sign-in sheet. Penny would hate it.

CLOSE.text: I close my eyes and listen to the silence. No notifications. No alerts. Just the mountain breathing.

PUSH.text: I lean on the railing. It creaks. I stop leaning on the railing.

PULL.text: The view tugs at something inside. A longing for simplicity. And breakfast. Mostly breakfast.

GIVE.text: The mountains gave me perspective. I've got nothing for them. They seem fine with that.

LOOK.text: The path leads back down. To the lab. To the world. To whatever comes next.

then.text: I take the first step down the mountain. Gerald would be proud. Probably.

else.text: Not yet. That NOW HIRING sign is staring at me.

TALK.text: I ask the path where it goes. It goes down. Paths are honest like that.

PICK.text: A smooth stone, worn by footsteps. I leave it. My pockets have done enough this week.

OPEN.text: The path is open. No keypad. No security question. DOORIS would find it reckless.

CLOSE.text: I don't want to close this path. It leads somewhere new. Somewhere without charts.

PUSH.text: I'm not pushing a path. I tried that with a pizza box once. It went badly.

PULL.text: Downhill is easier than uphill. My knees disagree, but my knees weren't consulted.

GIVE.text: I give the mountain one last look. It doesn't look back. Mountains are terrible at goodbyes.

golden_token: I hold the token up to the sign. They're hiring builders, not investors. Huh.

then.text: NOW HIRING. And under it, my name. Smudged. Official.

else.text: A sign: 'NOW HIRING. Apply within. Bring your own pen.'

then.text: Already signed. Twice would look desperate.
Bring your own pen, it says. I happen to own a very specific pen.

else.text: No pen. There is a pencil on a string. I sign. Detective Dex. Zero cases. One job.

TALK.text: 'Hello, sign. About the job.' The sign keeps saying NOW HIRING. Persistent. I like that in a sign.

PICK.text: I'm not stealing the job sign. Bad look for a new hire. Also it won't fit next to my emotional baggage.

OPEN.text: The sign doesn't open. It's a sign. I've opened enough envelopes this week.

CLOSE.text: Can't close a sign. It's open for business. Very open. Suspiciously open.

PUSH.text: I push the sign. It wobbles but holds. Somebody hammered it in with real conviction.

PULL.text: I pull the sign. It resists. If I break it before I'm hired, Penny will put it in my file.

GIVE.text: The sign wants applicants, not gifts. My resume says 'Zero cases.' I'll lead with my handwriting.

LOOK.text: Birds. And one duck. Not Gerald. Gerald doesn't fly. Gerald floats.

USE.text: I wave at the birds. One dips lower, as if waving back. Probably a coincidence. I'm keeping it.

TALK.text: I call out to the birds: 'Morning!' They fly higher. The moths would have stayed.

PICK.text: I can't pick up birds. They have wings. That's their whole counter-argument.

OPEN.text: I open my arms to the sky. For a moment I feel like I could fly. Then I remember the cliff.

CLOSE.text: I close my eyes and listen to the birds. Nobody is trying to sell me anything. Lovely.

PUSH.text: Can't push birds. They're already moving. Faster than me. Everything is, apparently.

PULL.text: The birds are out of reach. Which is how the birds like it.

GIVE.text: I have nothing for the birds. Gerald gets the breadcrumbs. Seniority.

LOOK.text: Tall pines line the mountainside. Patient, silent, completely calm. I could learn a thing or two.

USE.text: I lean against a pine. The bark is rough. I get sap on my coat. Adrian's coat. Sorry, Adrian.

TALK.text: 'Nice view up there?' A pinecone hits my head. I'll take that as a yes.

PICK.text: Pinecones everywhere. I leave them. My inventory is a crime scene already.

OPEN.text: I peel open a pinecone. Seeds inside. Twelve of them. I'm NOT writing them down. ...Progress.

CLOSE.text: I set the pinecone down. It closes up in the cold. Same, pinecone. Same.

PUSH.text: I push a tree. It doesn't budge. Trees have excellent boundaries.

PULL.text: I pull a low branch. It snaps back and slaps me. Fair. I'd slap me too.

GIVE.text: The trees give me oxygen. I give them nothing. They don't keep score. Refreshing.

then.text: Already signed. Twice would look desperate.

else.text: I sign with the Mt. Gox pen. It leaks all over my name.
Still leaking. Still useful. There's hope for all of us.
Detective Dex. Zero cases. One job.
Sunrise. Not a green candle. Not a breakout. Just... a sunrise.
The moths from the lamp fly past me, straight at the sun. Ambitious.
Dex. Penny. HR has approved your hiring.
else.speaker: Penny

else.text: Also, DOORIS has something to say. I patched her through.
else.speaker: Penny

else.text: Good morning, Dex. Voice match: 100 %. Welcome home.
else.speaker: DOORIS

else.text: She said my name. Not 'unknown wallet'. My name.
